name: SIA Project 25 26
description:
In the Municipality of Turin, a system called Participium is being developed — an information 
system that enables citizen participation in the management of urban environments. It allows 
citizens to interact with the public administration by reporting inconveniences and malfunctions 
found in the city (e.g., potholes in the asphalt, sidewalks with architectural barriers, garbage in the 
streets, broken streetlights, etc.). An example of a similar information system is IRIS in Venice: 
https://iris.sad.ve.it/. The system, once developed, will be made available as open-source 
software to all Italian public administrations through the portal https://developers.italia.it/.

A. REPORTS 
Citizens can submit reports only if they have registered in the system with a username, first name, 
and last name. Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. 
The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through 
that link. Once registered, a citizen can submit reports by selecting a point on the map of Turin 
(which will be saved with latitude and longitude values) and filling in a problem form with the 
following mandatory fields: title, textual description, category (chosen from a predefined list). It is 
also mandatory to attach one or more photos (up to 3 per report, with each photo stored with its 
file path on the server). The possible problem categories are: 
• Waterworks – Drinking water 
• Architectural Barriers 
• Sewerage 
• Public Lighting 
• Waste 
• Road Signs and Traffic Lights 
• Roads and Urban Furniture 
• Public Green Areas and Playgrounds 
• Other 
After entering all the information and the pictures, the system asks the citizen whether they want 
the report to be anonymous (the name will not appear in the public list of all reports).  

B. REPORT LIFECYCLE 
Once submitted, the report is in the “Pending Approval” state until the Organization Office of the 
Municipality of Turin performs a preliminary review of citizen reports, marking them as accepted 
or rejected. The possible states for a report are: Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, 
Suspended, Rejected. After approval, accepted reports move to the “In Progress” state, at which 
point they are assigned to the technical office responsible, based on the problem category. Once 
the intervention is planned, the state changes to “Work in Progress”, indicating that the issue 
resolution has started. In some cases, for organizational or technical reasons, the report can be 
set to “Suspended”, awaiting further evaluation or resources. When the problem is solved, the 
technical office updates the status and closes the report. In case of rejection, a written explanation 
from the Organization Office is mandatory (see next section).  
If the intervention must be carried out by maintenance personnel from an external company (for 
example, Enel X for Public Lighting, or company Y for specific reports based on their content), 
two cases are possible: - Case 1: The company has access to Participium. In this case, the technical office assigns the 
report to users from the corresponding company. External maintenance personnel can move the 
report from Assigned to In Progress. Staff from the technical office and external maintenance 
workers can exchange information and comments through the report, but these are not visible to 
the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens). Once the work is completed, the external maintainer 
can mark the report as resolved. 
Note: Automatic assignment of all reports in a certain category to the external company 
(bypassing the initial review by the public relations officer of the municipality) is possible only if 
previously configured by the municipal administrator. - Case 2: The company does NOT have access to Participium. In this case, the external company 
updates the technical office outside Participium, and once the problems are solved, a staff 
member from the technical office will manually move the report to the Resolved state. 


C. CITIZEN UPDATES 
To strengthen trust between citizens and institutions, the citizen can receive updates regarding 
their own reports through various channels. First, at every state change, the citizen receives a 
notification on the platform with the corresponding update. Furthermore, municipal operators 
updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can 
reply. The system must allow this functionality to be accessible by external chatbots as well. Each 
time the citizen receives a notification on the platform, they also get an email (this option can be 
disabled in the user settings panel, where they can also upload a personal photo). 
Moreover, after the approval phase, accepted reports immediately become visible on the 
Participium portal: they appear both on an interactive map of Turin, geolocated based on the 
citizen’s selected point, and in a summary table that allows filtering and sorting reports by 
category, status, or date. In both views, the reporter’s name (“anonymous” if that option was 
chosen) and the report title are displayed. Clicking on the title opens a page with the description.  
Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table. Once logged into 
Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications (following the 
same rules as for their own reports). 


D. STATISTICS 
The system allows viewing public and private statistics. Public statistics are visible in a dedicated 
section of the website and concern the number of reports per category, and trends over day, week, 
or month. They are also visible to non-registered users. In the private section, accessible only to 
administrators, it is possible to view, in addition to the public statistics, charts and tables.

highLevelGoals: Provide a streamlined and user-friendly interface for citizens to register and submit reports about urban issues, ensuring accessibility and ease of use.
Establish a clear and efficient workflow for municipal operators to review, approve, and manage citizen reports, ensuring timely responses and accountability.
Ensure effective collaboration with external maintenance personnel to address reported issues promptly and efficiently, maintaining communication throughout the resolution process.
Equip municipal administrators with tools to configure system settings and manage the assignment of reports to appropriate personnel, optimizing operational efficiency.
Allow non-registered users to access and view reports and statistics, fostering transparency and encouraging community engagement in urban management.
lowLevelGoals: Allow citizens to create a new account by providing personal information and verifying their identity.
Allow citizens to submit a new report about an urban issue through a form interface.
Enable citizens to upload images or videos related to their report to provide additional context.
Allow citizens to view the status of their submitted reports and any updates made by municipal operators.
Enable municipal operators to access and review submitted reports for validity and urgency.
Allow municipal operators to examine the details of a report to determine its validity and urgency.
Allow municipal operators to approve a report after review, marking it as valid and ready for action.
Enable municipal operators to reject a report and provide feedback to the citizen about the rejection reason.
Allow municipal operators to assign approved reports to external maintenance personnel for resolution.
Enable external maintenance personnel to update the status of a report as they work on it, providing real-time updates to municipal operators.
Allow external maintenance personnel to mark a report as resolved once the issue has been addressed, notifying municipal operators and citizens.
Enable municipal administrators to modify system settings such as report categories and notification preferences.
Allow municipal administrators to assign specific reports to designated municipal operators for review and action.
Allow non-registered users to access and view a list of reports and relevant statistics without needing to register.

branch_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enhance citizen engagement and participation in urban management through a comprehensive reporting system.
branch_001.rationale: The low-level goals collectively aim to empower citizens by facilitating account creation, enabling them to report urban issues, provide supporting media, and track the progress of their reports. This integration fosters a participatory approach to urban management.

branch_002.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Facilitate the effective management and resolution of municipal reports by operators.
branch_002.rationale: All the low-level goals focus on the processes involved in reviewing, approving, rejecting, and assigning municipal reports, which are essential for ensuring that issues reported by citizens are addressed efficiently and effectively.

branch_003.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enhance communication and transparency between external maintenance personnel and municipal operators regarding report statuses.
branch_003.rationale: Both low-level goals focus on improving the flow of information related to maintenance reports, ensuring that updates and resolutions are communicated effectively to municipal operators and citizens, thereby fostering accountability and responsiveness in municipal services.

branch_004.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enhance the management and customization of municipal reporting systems for administrators.
branch_004.rationale: Both low-level goals focus on empowering municipal administrators with the ability to tailor the reporting system to their needs, ensuring that reports are relevant and actionable by assigning them to specific operators.

branch_005.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enhance accessibility of reports and statistics for all users.
branch_005.rationale: This goal encompasses the intention to provide open access to information, promoting transparency and user engagement without barriers such as registration.

branch_001.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Facilitate Citizen Reporting' accurately captures the primary functional intention of the Citizens actor as described in the project description. The text explicitly details the registration and report submission process (Section A), which constitutes the core interaction for this actor. The goal is supported by the documentation, reasonably scoped to the actor's main contribution, and faithful to the system's purpose. The reconstructed goal is too broad and abstract ('Enhance citizen engagement...'), whereas the original goal focuses on the specific functional capability provided to the actor. Therefore, the original goal should be kept. The current LLGs are incomplete and partially misleading regarding the scope of the parent HLG 'Facilitate Citizen Reporting'. 
1. Incompleteness: The parent HLG implies the entire process of reporting. The current LLGs miss critical steps defined in the requirements, such as 'Select Location on Map' (mandatory for submission), 'Choose Anonymity Option' (explicitly required after filling the form), and 'Verify Email' (part of the registration validity). 
2. Misleading/Too Operational: 'Attach Media to Report' is listed as a separate high-level goal, but the requirements state it is a mandatory field within the submission process, not a distinct user goal parallel to submitting. Separating it suggests it's optional or a separate workflow, which is misleading. 
3. Scope Mismatch: 'View Submitted Reports' is included, but the parent HLG is specifically about *facilitating the act of reporting* (registration + submission). Viewing status is part of the 'Report Lifecycle' or 'Citizen Updates' phase, which might be better covered by a different HLG or should be clearly distinguished. However, given the HLG description mentions 'streamlined... interface... to register and submit', the focus should be on the creation flow. The current set mixes creation steps with post-creation viewing without covering the mandatory intermediate steps (location, anonymity). 
4. Missing Actor Context: The HLG actor is 'Citizens'. The LLGs correctly identify this, but the decomposition fails to capture the mandatory constraints (e.g., email confirmation) that define the 'valid' registration mentioned in the HLG description.

The reconstructed goal is too broad and abstract ('Enhance citizen engagement...'), whereas the original goal focuses on the specific functional capability provided to the actor. Therefore, the original goal should be kept.

low_level_evaluation.regeneration_feedback:
The decomposition is incomplete and structurally flawed. 
1. Merge 'Attach Media' into 'Submit Report' or make it a sub-step, as it is a mandatory part of the submission form, not a separate goal. 
2. Add 'Verify Email Address' as a distinct LLG under Registration, as the system requires confirmation before the user can use the system. 
3. Add 'Select Issue Location' as a distinct LLG, as selecting a point on the map is a mandatory step before filling the form. 
4. Add 'Choose Anonymity Preference' as a distinct LLG, as the system explicitly asks this after form completion. 
5. Consider removing 'View Submitted Reports' if the HLG is strictly about the *submission* process, or rename the HLG to 'Manage Citizen Reports' if viewing is intended. Given the HLG name 'Facilitate Citizen Reporting', it likely focuses on the creation. If viewing is kept, ensure the HLG description is updated or the LLG is justified as part of the 'feedback loop' of reporting. However, based on the text 'register and submit', the primary focus is creation. 
6. Ensure 'Register Citizen Account' includes the email verification step or has a child goal for it.

branch_002.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Enhance Report Review Process' is supported by the project description, specifically section B (Report Lifecycle), which details the workflow for Municipal Operators (Organization Office and Technical Office) to review, approve, reject, and manage reports. The goal accurately reflects the actor's responsibility to ensure accountability and timely responses through this workflow. It is not too generic, as it specifically targets the 'Review Process' which is a distinct and critical phase described in the text. It is not too narrow, as it encompasses the broader management aspect implied by the lifecycle states. Therefore, it should be kept. The current LLGs are incomplete and partially inconsistent with the project description. 
1. Incompleteness: The HLG mentions 'manage citizen reports', but the LLGs only cover the initial review (Access, Review, Approve, Reject) and assignment. They miss critical management steps described in Section B, such as updating the status to 'Work in Progress', 'Suspended', or 'Resolved' (especially for external companies without system access, where the operator must manually update the status). 
2. Inconsistency/Unsupported: The LLG 'Reject Report' states it provides feedback to the citizen. While Section B says a written explanation is mandatory, it does not explicitly state this feedback is sent *to the citizen* via the system in the rejection step (though Section C mentions notifications, the rejection explanation is a specific administrative requirement). More importantly, the LLG 'Assign Report to Maintenance Personnel' is too narrow; it only covers external personnel. Section B states that after approval, reports are assigned to the 'technical office responsible' based on category. This internal assignment is a key part of the workflow before any external assignment might occur. 
3. Missing Goals: The workflow includes states like 'In Progress', 'Work in Progress', 'Suspended', and 'Resolved'. The current LLGs do not cover the transitions to these states by the municipal operators (e.g., marking as Work in Progress, Suspending, or Resolving for non-connected external companies). 
Therefore, the LLGs need regeneration to fully decompose the 'Enhance Report Review Process' HLG, covering the entire lifecycle management by municipal operators.

low_level_evaluation.regeneration_feedback:
The current LLGs focus heavily on the initial approval/rejection phase but fail to cover the subsequent management of the report lifecycle by municipal operators. Specifically:
1. Add LLGs for managing the report status after approval, such as 'Assign Report to Internal Technical Office', 'Update Report Status to Work in Progress', 'Suspend Report', and 'Resolve Report' (specifically for cases where external companies do not have system access).
2. Refine 'Reject Report' to ensure it aligns with the requirement of providing a written explanation, but clarify if this is an internal record or a citizen notification based on Section C.
3. Ensure the decomposition covers the full scope of 'manage' as implied by the HLG, including the handover to external entities and the final closure of reports.

branch_003.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Coordinate Issue Resolution' accurately captures the functional intention of the External Maintenance Personnel actor as described in Section B (Case 1). The text explicitly states that these personnel can move reports from 'Assigned' to 'In Progress', exchange information/comments with the technical office, and mark reports as 'resolved'. This constitutes coordinating the resolution of the issue. The goal is supported by the documentation, reasonably scoped to the actor's responsibilities, and faithful to the project description. The reconstructed goal focuses heavily on 'transparency' and 'communication' which are means to an end, whereas the original goal correctly identifies the primary business outcome (resolving the issue) facilitated by that coordination. Therefore, the original goal should be kept. The current LLGs are incomplete and partially inconsistent with the project description. 
1. Incompleteness: The parent HLG 'Coordinate Issue Resolution' implies a two-way collaboration. The current LLGs only cover the external personnel's actions (updating status, marking resolved) but miss the critical communication aspect mentioned in the description: 'Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report'. This exchange is a key part of 'coordinating' and 'maintaining communication'.
2. Inconsistency/Misleading: The LLG 'Complete Report Resolution' states it notifies 'citizens'. However, the description explicitly states that comments and internal exchanges are 'not visible to the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens)'. While the citizen receives a notification of the state change (via email/platform notification as per section C), the LLG description implies a direct notification from the resolution action itself which might be misleading regarding the content visibility. More importantly, the 'Coordinate' aspect is missing the municipal operator's side of the interaction (assigning, commenting).
3. Scope: The parent HLG is about 'collaboration'. The current LLGs are purely operational steps for the external actor. They do not fully decompose the 'collaboration' goal, which involves both parties. Therefore, they are too narrow and incomplete.

Section B explicitly mentions that automatic assignment to external companies is 'possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator,' supporting the 'System Configuration' aspect. The actor description explicitly states they 'oversee the assignment of reports,' and Section B details the workflow where technical offices (under administrative oversight) assign reports to personnel or external companies, supporting the 'Report Assignment' aspect. The project description specifies that reports can also be assigned to external companies (Case 1) and that automatic assignment rules can be configured by administrators. The current LLGs do not cover the configuration of these assignment rules or the assignment to external entities.
2. Misleading/Too Narrow: The LLG 'Configure System Settings' is too vague. The project description highlights specific configuration needs, such as enabling automatic assignment for external companies and managing notification preferences. The current description does not reflect the specific operational impact of these configurations on the report lifecycle.
3. Missing Goal: There is no LLG for managing the configuration of external company access or automatic assignment rules, which is a key part of 'optimizing operational efficiency' mentioned in the HLG description.

branch_001.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Facilitate Citizen Reporting' accurately captures the core functional intention of the Citizens actor as described in the project description (Section A). The description explicitly details the registration and report submission process, including mandatory fields, photo attachments, and map selection. The goal is supported by the text, reasonably scoped to the actor's primary contribution, and faithful to the reconstruction. It is not too generic, ambiguous, or incorrectly scoped. Therefore, it should be kept. The current LLGs are incomplete and partially inconsistent with the project description. 
1. Incompleteness: The HLG 'Facilitate Citizen Reporting' implies the entire process of reporting. The current LLGs cover registration and submission but miss critical aspects of the 'reporting' experience defined in the text, such as the mandatory fields (title, description, category), the specific constraint on photos (up to 3), and the immediate feedback/confirmation mechanism which is part of the user's reporting journey. More importantly, the HLG description mentions 'streamlined and user-friendly interface... to register and submit'. The current LLGs break this down but miss the specific data entry steps (Select Category, Write Description) which are distinct from just 'Submit New Report' if we are decomposing the *interface* usage. However, the bigger issue is that 'Submit New Report' is too high-level if it's meant to be a leaf node alongside 'Select Issue Location'. Usually, 'Submit' is the final action. The decomposition should likely include 'Fill Report Details' (Title, Description, Category) and 'Attach Photos' as distinct steps before submission, or 'Submit New Report' should be the parent of those. Given the current flat list, 'Submit New Report' is too broad/operational if it encompasses the whole form filling, but too narrow if it's just the click. 
2. Inconsistency/Misleading: 'Login to Citizen Account' is not a sub-goal of 'Facilitate Citizen Reporting' in the context of the *first-time* reporting flow described in the HLG description ('register and submit'). While login is needed for subsequent reports, the HLG focuses on the initial engagement. However, the main issue is that the current LLGs do not fully capture the *constraints* and *specifics* of the reporting process defined in Section A (e.g., mandatory fields, photo limits). 
3. Missing LLGs: The current list lacks LLGs for 'Select Problem Category' and 'Write Problem Description', which are mandatory parts of the reporting process. 'Submit New Report' is vague. 
4. Therefore, the decomposition is incomplete and too operational/vague in places. It needs regeneration to properly reflect the specific steps of the reporting form (Category, Description, Photos, Anonymity) as distinct low-level goals or to group them more logically under a 'Create Report' LLG if the current granularity is too fine. Given the instruction to regenerate if incomplete or too operational, and the fact that key mandatory steps (Category, Description) are missing as distinct LLGs or are buried in a vague 'Submit' LLG, regeneration is required.

branch_002.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Enhance Report Review Process' is supported by the project description, specifically section B (Report Lifecycle), which details the workflow for Municipal Operators (Organization Office and Technical Office) to review, approve, reject, and manage reports. The goal accurately reflects the actor's responsibility to ensure accountability and timely responses through this workflow. It is not too generic, as it specifically targets the 'Review Process' which is a distinct and critical phase described in the text. It is not too narrow, as it encompasses the broader management aspect implied by the lifecycle states. Therefore, it should be kept. The current LLGs are incomplete and partially inconsistent with the project description. 
1. Incompleteness: The HLG mentions 'manage citizen reports', but the LLGs only cover the initial review (Access, Review, Approve, Reject) and assignment. They miss critical management steps described in Section B, such as updating the status to 'Work in Progress', 'Suspended', or 'Resolved' (especially for external companies without system access, where the operator must manually update the status). 
2. Inconsistency/Unsupported: The LLG 'Reject Report' states it provides feedback to the citizen. While Section B says a written explanation is mandatory, it does not explicitly state this feedback is sent *to the citizen* via the system in the rejection step (though Section C mentions notifications, the rejection explanation is a specific administrative requirement). More importantly, the LLG 'Assign Report to Maintenance Personnel' is too narrow; it only covers external personnel. Section B states that after approval, reports are assigned to the 'technical office responsible' based on category. This internal assignment is a key part of the workflow before any external assignment might occur. 
3. Missing Goals: The workflow includes states like 'In Progress', 'Work in Progress', 'Suspended', and 'Resolved'. The current LLGs do not cover the transitions to these states by the municipal operators (e.g., marking as Work in Progress, Suspending, or Resolving for non-connected external companies). 
Therefore, the LLGs need regeneration to fully decompose the 'Enhance Report Review Process' HLG, covering the entire lifecycle management by municipal operators.

The original High-Level Goal 'Coordinate Issue Resolution' accurately captures the functional intention of the External Maintenance Personnel actor as described in Section B (Case 1). The text explicitly states that external personnel can move reports from 'Assigned' to 'In Progress', exchange information/comments with the technical office, and mark reports as 'resolved'. This constitutes coordinating the resolution of the issue. The goal is supported by the documentation, reasonably scoped to the actor's responsibilities, and faithful to the project description. The reconstructed goal focuses on 'transparency' and 'communication' which are aspects of the coordination, but the original goal better encapsulates the primary functional outcome (resolving the issue) rather than just the means (communication). Therefore, the original goal should be kept. The current LLGs are incomplete and partially inconsistent with the project description.

The current LLGs only cover the external personnel's actions (updating status, marking resolved) but miss the critical communication aspect mentioned in the description: 'Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report'. This exchange is a key part of 'coordinating' and 'maintaining communication'.
2. Inconsistency/Misleading: The LLG 'Complete Report Resolution' states it notifies 'citizens'. However, the description explicitly states that comments and internal exchanges are 'not visible to the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens)'. While the citizen receives a notification of the state change (via email/platform notification as per section C), the LLG description implies a direct notification from the resolution action itself which might be misleading regarding the content visibility. More importantly, the 'Coordinate' aspect is missing the municipal operator's side of the interaction (assigning, commenting).
3. Scope: The parent HLG is about 'collaboration'. The current LLGs are purely operational steps for the external actor. They do not fully decompose the 'collaboration' goal, which involves both parties. Therefore, regeneration is needed to include the communication/exchange of information aspect and to ensure the decomposition covers the full scope of 'coordination' between the external personnel and the municipal operators.

branch_001.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Facilitate Citizen Reporting' accurately captures the core functional intention of the Citizens actor as described in the project specification. The text explicitly details the registration process and the submission of reports (Section A) as the primary means for citizens to interact with the system. The goal is supported by the documentation, reasonably scoped to the actor's main contribution, and faithful to the reconstructed goal. It is not too generic, ambiguous, or incorrectly scoped. The current LLGs are incomplete and partially misleading. 
1. Incompleteness: The HLG 'Facilitate Citizen Reporting' implies the entire process of reporting. The current LLGs cover registration and submission but miss critical aspects of the 'reporting' experience defined in the project description, such as the mandatory fields (title, description, category) and the specific constraint of attaching photos (up to 3). While 'Submit New Report' exists, it is too high-level and doesn't decompose the specific data entry requirements mandated by the system (e.g., selecting from a predefined category list). 
2. Misleading/Unsupported: The LLG 'Attach Media to Report' mentions 'images or videos', but the project description explicitly states 'attach one or more photos (up to 3 per report... each photo stored with its file path)'. There is no mention of video support. This makes the LLG misleading regarding system capabilities. 
3. Granularity: 'Select Issue Location' and 'Choose Anonymity Preference' are good decompositions. However, 'Submit New Report' is too broad and overlaps with the other steps. A better decomposition would separate the data entry steps (Fill Report Details, Select Category, Attach Photos) to ensure all mandatory fields are covered as distinct goals or sub-goals. 
4. Missing Context: The HLG description mentions 'ensuring accessibility and ease of use'. The current LLGs do not explicitly address the 'ease of use' aspect regarding the map interaction or the form structure, though this is often implicit. The main issue is the inaccuracy in media types and the lack of decomposition for the specific mandatory fields (Category, Title, Description) which are central to the reporting process.

1. Remove 'Attach Media to Report' as it incorrectly includes 'videos'. Replace with 'Attach Photos to Report' specifying the limit of 3 photos. 
2. Decompose 'Submit New Report' into more specific LLGs that reflect the mandatory fields: 'Enter Report Title and Description', 'Select Problem Category', and 'Select Issue Location on Map'.

branch_002.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Enhance Report Review Process' is supported by the project description, specifically section B (Report Lifecycle), which details the workflow for Municipal Operators (Organization Office and Technical Office) to review, approve, reject, and manage reports. The goal accurately reflects the actor's responsibility to ensure accountability and timely responses through this workflow. It is not too generic, as it specifically targets the 'Review Process' which is a distinct and critical phase described in the text. It is not too narrow, as it encompasses the broader management aspect implied by the lifecycle states. Therefore, it should be kept. The current LLGs are incomplete and partially inconsistent with the project description. 
1. Incompleteness: The HLG mentions 'manage citizen reports', but the LLGs only cover the initial review (Access, Review, Approve, Reject) and assignment. They miss critical management steps described in Section B, such as updating the status to 'Work in Progress', 'Suspended', or 'Resolved', and handling the specific workflows for external companies (Case 1 and Case 2). 
2. Inconsistency/Unsupported: The LLG 'Reject Report' states it provides feedback to the citizen. While Section B says a written explanation is mandatory, it does not explicitly state this feedback is sent directly to the citizen via the system in the rejection step (though Section C mentions updates, the rejection reason is a specific administrative requirement). More importantly, the LLGs fail to capture the 'Assignment' nuance where reports are assigned to technical offices based on category, and then potentially to external companies. The current 'Assign Report' LLG is too narrow as it only mentions external personnel, ignoring the internal technical office assignment which is the primary step after approval. 
3. Missing Goals: There is no LLG for 'Update Report Status' (e.g., to Work in Progress, Suspended, Resolved) which is a core part of the 'management' aspect of the HLG. There is no LLG for 'Manage External Company Interactions' (comments, status updates from external users). 

Therefore, the LLGs need regeneration to fully decompose the HLG.

The current LLGs focus heavily on the initial review phase but neglect the ongoing management and resolution phases described in the HLG and project description. Specifically:
1. Add LLGs for updating report statuses (e.g., 'Mark Report as Work in Progress', 'Suspend Report', 'Resolve Report') as these are key management actions.
2. Refine the assignment LLG to reflect the two-step process: first assigning to the internal technical office based on category, and then potentially to external companies.

branch_001.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Facilitate Citizen Reporting' accurately captures the core functional intention of the Citizens actor as described in the project description. The text explicitly details the registration and report submission process (Section A), which constitutes the primary interaction for this actor. The goal is supported by the documentation, reasonably scoped to the actor's main purpose, and not overly generic or ambiguous. The reconstructed goal is essentially a paraphrase of the original, so no rewriting is necessary. The current LLGs are incomplete and too operational. 
1. Incomplete: The HLG 'Facilitate Citizen Reporting' implies the entire process of reporting. The current LLGs miss critical steps defined in the requirements: 
   - Registration requires email confirmation (LLG 'Register User' only mentions creating an account, missing the validation step which is a prerequisite for using the system).
   - The report submission requires mandatory photos (LLG 'Attach Photos' exists but is separate; however, the flow is fragmented).
   - Most importantly, the HLG is about 'Reporting', but the current LLGs treat 'Login' as a primary goal. While login is necessary, the core value is the submission. 
   - The current LLGs are a list of atomic actions (API calls) rather than user goals. For example, 'Enter Report Title' and 'Select Category' are sub-steps of 'Compose Report'. 
2. Too Operational: Descriptions like 'through a registration API' or 'through a report title and description API' are implementation details, not user goals. Goals should be 'Register Account', 'Compose Report', 'Submit Report'.
3. Missing Context: The HLG mentions 'accessibility and ease of use'. The current LLGs do not reflect the user-centric nature of the interaction (e.g., selecting a point on a map is a key part of the 'ease of use' for location, but it's buried in a technical API description).

Therefore, the LLGs need to be regenerated to better reflect the user's high-level goals (Register, Compose, Submit) and ensure all mandatory steps (like email confirmation) are captured as part of the registration goal or a distinct validation goal if necessary, though typically 'Register' implies the successful completion of the process. The current decomposition is too granular and technical. LLG regeneration limit reached; keeping the latest LLGs.

branch_001.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Facilitate Citizen Reporting' accurately captures the core functional intention of the Citizens actor as described in the project description. The text explicitly details the registration and report submission process (Section A), which constitutes the primary interaction for this actor. The goal is supported by the documentation, reasonably scoped to the actor's main purpose, and not overly generic or ambiguous. The reconstructed goal is essentially a paraphrase of the original, so no rewriting is necessary. The current LLGs are incomplete and too operational. 
1. Incomplete: The HLG 'Facilitate Citizen Reporting' implies the entire process of reporting. The current LLGs miss critical steps defined in the requirements: 
   - Registration requires email confirmation (LLG 'Register User' only mentions creating an account, missing the validation step which is a prerequisite for using the system).
   - The report submission requires mandatory photos (LLG 'Attach Photos' exists but is separate; however, the flow is fragmented).
   - Most importantly, the HLG is about 'Reporting', but the current LLGs treat 'Login' as a primary goal. While login is necessary, the core value is the submission. 
   - The current LLGs are a list of atomic actions (API calls) rather than user goals. For example, 'Enter Report Title' and 'Select Category' are sub-steps of 'Compose Report'. 
2. Too Operational: Descriptions like 'through a registration API' or 'through a report title and description API' are implementation details, not user goals. Goals should be 'Register Account', 'Compose Report', 'Submit Report'.
3. Missing Context: The HLG mentions 'accessibility and ease of use'. The current LLGs do not reflect the user-centric nature of the interaction (e.g., selecting a point on a map is a key part of the 'ease of use' for location, but it's buried in a technical API description).

Therefore, the LLGs need to be regenerated to better reflect the user's high-level goals (Register, Compose, Submit) and ensure all mandatory steps (like email confirmation) are captured as part of the registration goal or a distinct validation goal if necessary, though typically 'Register' implies the successful completion of the process. The current decomposition is too granular and technical. LLG regeneration limit reached; keeping the latest LLGs.

branch_002.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Enhance Report Review Process' is supported by the project description, specifically section B (Report Lifecycle), which details the workflow for municipal operators (Organization Office and Technical Office) to review, approve, reject, and manage reports. The goal accurately reflects the actor's responsibility to ensure accountability (via rejection explanations and status tracking) and responsiveness (via state transitions). It is not too generic, as it specifically targets the review and management workflow defined in the text. It is not too narrow, as it covers the entire lifecycle management aspect for this actor. Therefore, it should be kept. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) are incomplete and partially inconsistent with the parent High-Level Goal (HLG) 'Enhance Report Review Process' and the project description. 

1. **Incompleteness**: The HLG focuses on the workflow for municipal operators to review, approve, and manage reports. The current LLGs miss critical steps defined in the 'Report Lifecycle' section, specifically: 
   - Assigning reports to external companies (Case 1) or managing the workflow when external companies do not have access (Case 2). 
   - The specific action of moving a report to 'Resolved' status, which is a key part of the management workflow.
   - The distinction between 'In Progress' (assigned) and 'Work in Progress' (intervention started) is blurred or missing in the current LLGs.

2. **Inconsistency/Misleading**: 
   - 'Submit Citizen Report' is an action performed by Citizens, not Municipal Operators. While it is a prerequisite for the review process, it is not a sub-goal of the operator's review workflow itself. Including it under an HLG for 'Municipal Operators' is misleading regarding the actor.
   - 'Generate Report Summary' and 'View Report History' are more related to statistics and auditing (Section D) rather than the core 'Review and Manage' workflow described in the HLG. While useful, they are not central to the 'Review Process' HLG.
   - 'Notify External Maintainers' is vague. The system description specifies that assignment happens via the system (Case 1) or manual update (Case 2). The LLG should reflect the assignment action rather than just notification.

3. **Too Operational/Narrow**: Some LLGs like 'Add Comments' are too granular and operational. They should be part of a broader 'Manage Report Details' or 'Collaborate on Report' goal.

Therefore, the LLGs need to be regenerated to accurately reflect the Municipal Operator's responsibilities in the review and management lifecycle, excluding citizen actions and focusing on the specific states and assignments described in the text.

low_level_evaluation.regeneration_feedback:
Regenerate LLGs to strictly focus on the Municipal Operator's actions within the report lifecycle. 
1. Remove 'Submit Citizen Report' as it is a Citizen goal.
2. Include specific goals for: 
   - Reviewing pending reports (checking validity/completeness).
   - Approving reports (moving to 'In Progress' and assigning to technical office).
   - Rejecting reports (with mandatory explanation).
   - Managing external assignments (assigning to external company users if they have access).
   - Updating status to 'Work in Progress', 'Suspended', or 'Resolved' based on technical office feedback.
   - Communicating with citizens (sending messages/updates) as part of the management process.

branch_003.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Coordinate Issue Resolution' accurately captures the functional intention of the External Maintenance Personnel actor as described in Section B (Case 1). The text explicitly states that these personnel can move reports from 'Assigned' to 'In Progress', exchange information/comments with the technical office, and mark reports as 'resolved'. This constitutes coordinating the resolution of the issue. The goal is supported by the documentation, reasonably scoped to the actor's responsibilities, and faithful to the project description. The reconstructed goal focuses heavily on 'transparency' and 'communication' which are means to an end, whereas the original goal correctly identifies the primary business outcome (resolving the issue) facilitated by that coordination. Therefore, the original goal should be kept. The current LLGs are incomplete and partially inconsistent with the project description. 
1. Incompleteness: The parent HLG 'Coordinate Issue Resolution' implies a two-way collaboration. The current LLGs only cover the external personnel's actions (updating status, marking resolved) but miss the critical communication aspect mentioned in the description: 'Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report'. This exchange is a key part of 'coordinating' and 'maintaining communication'.
2. Inconsistency/Misleading: The LLG 'Complete Report Resolution' states it notifies 'citizens'. However, the description explicitly states that comments and internal exchanges are 'not visible to the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens)'. While the citizen receives a notification of the state change (via email/platform notification as per section C), the LLG description implies a direct notification from the resolution action itself which might be misleading regarding the content visibility. More importantly, the 'Coordinate' aspect is missing the municipal operator's side of the interaction (assigning, commenting).
3. Scope: The parent HLG is about 'collaboration'. The current LLGs are purely operational steps for the external actor. They do not fully decompose the 'collaboration' goal, which involves both parties. Therefore, they are too narrow and incomplete.

branch_004.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Manage System Configuration and Report Assignment' is well-supported by the project description. Section B explicitly mentions that automatic assignment to external companies is 'possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator,' supporting the 'System Configuration' aspect. The actor description explicitly states they 'oversee the assignment of reports,' and Section B details the workflow where technical offices (under administrative oversight) assign reports to personnel or external companies, supporting the 'Report Assignment' aspect. The goal is reasonably scoped for the actor and faithful to the text. The bottom-up reconstruction is too generic and loses the specific functional intent of configuration and assignment. The current LLGs are incomplete and partially misleading regarding the scope of the parent HLG. 
1. Incompleteness: The parent HLG explicitly mentions 'Report Assignment'. The current LLG 'Assign Reports to Operators' only covers assignment to municipal operators. The project description specifies a critical workflow for 'External Companies' (Case 1 and Case 2) and the configuration of automatic assignment to these external entities. The current LLGs do not cover the management of external company access or the configuration of automatic routing rules, which are key parts of 'managing assignment' in this context.
2. Misleading/Too Narrow: The LLG 'Configure System Settings' is vague. While it mentions categories and notifications, the project description highlights specific configuration needs like enabling/disabling email notifications, managing user settings, and crucially, configuring the automatic assignment of reports to external companies. The current LLG does not capture the operational nuance of configuring the assignment logic itself, which is a core part of the parent goal.
3. Missing Actor/Scope: The parent HLG actor is 'Municipal Administrators'. The current LLGs imply they do the assigning. However, the description states that 'Technical Office' assigns reports to external companies or internal staff. The 'Municipal Administrator' configures the *rules* for this (e.g., 'automatic assignment... is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator'). Therefore, the LLG should reflect the configuration of assignment rules rather than the direct assignment action, or include a specific LLG for managing external company integrations/configurations. The current decomposition misses the 'Configuration of Assignment Rules' aspect entirely.

branch_001.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Facilitate Citizen Reporting' accurately captures the core functional intention of the Citizens actor as described in the project description (Section A). The description explicitly details the process of registration and report submission (selecting location, filling forms, attaching photos). The goal is supported by the text, reasonably scoped to the actor's primary contribution, and faithful to the reconstruction. It is not too generic, ambiguous, or incorrectly scoped. Therefore, it should be kept. The current LLGs are incomplete and too operational. 
1. Incomplete: The HLG 'Facilitate Citizen Reporting' implies the entire process of reporting. The current LLGs miss critical steps defined in the requirements: 
   - Registration requires email confirmation (LLG 'Register User' only mentions creating an account, missing the validation step which is a prerequisite for using the system).
   - The report submission requires mandatory photos (LLG 'Attach Photos' exists but is separate; however, the flow is fragmented).
   - Most importantly, the HLG is about 'Reporting', but the current LLGs treat 'Login' as a primary goal. While login is necessary, the core value is the submission. 
   - The current LLGs are a list of atomic actions (API calls) rather than user goals. For example, 'Enter Report Title' and 'Select Category' are sub-steps of 'Compose Report'. 
2. Too Operational: Descriptions like 'through a registration API' or 'through a report title and description API' are implementation details, not user goals. Goals should be 'Register Account', 'Compose Report', 'Submit Report'.
3. Missing Context: The HLG mentions 'streamlined and user-friendly interface'. The current LLGs do not reflect the user's perspective of filling out a form or interacting with a map as a cohesive task.

Therefore, the LLGs need to be regenerated to better reflect the user's high-level goals (Register, Compose, Submit) and include the necessary validation steps (Confirm Registration) to be complete.

branch_002.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Enhance Report Review Process' is too narrow. While the project description details the review process (Section B), the Municipal Operators' responsibilities extend significantly beyond just reviewing. They are responsible for assigning reports to technical offices, managing the lifecycle states (In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Resolved), handling external company assignments, and communicating with citizens (Section C). The bottom-up reconstruction 'Streamline the management and resolution of citizen reports' better captures the full scope of the actor's functional intention as described in the text. Therefore, the original goal should be rewritten to reflect the broader management and resolution responsibilities.

replacement_request.rationale: The original HLG focused narrowly on the 'review' phase. The reconstructed HLG broadens the scope to cover the entire lifecycle management (assignment, status updates, resolution) and communication handled by Municipal Operators. To generate the correct Low-Level Goals (LLGs), the request must explicitly include the requirements for assigning reports to technical offices or external companies, managing state transitions (Pending, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Resolved, Rejected), handling external company interactions (Case 1 and Case 2), and facilitating communication with citizens and external parties. The actor remains 'Municipal Operators' as defined.
replacement_request.generation_project_description: Municipal Operators are responsible for the end-to-end management of citizen reports within the Participium system. Upon submission, reports enter a 'Pending Approval' state. Operators must review these reports and either accept or reject them. If rejected, a written explanation is mandatory. If accepted, the report moves to 'In Progress' and is assigned to the relevant technical office based on the problem category (e.g., Waterworks, Public Lighting). Operators manage the report's lifecycle, updating statuses to 'Work in Progress' when intervention starts, 'Suspended' if resources are pending, or 'Resolved' when the issue is fixed. For reports requiring external maintenance companies, operators handle two scenarios: 1) If the company has system access, operators assign the report to the company's users, who can update statuses and communicate internally with operators; 2) If the company lacks access, operators manually update the status to 'Resolved' based on external updates. Operators also communicate with citizens via the platform's messaging system and notifications, ensuring transparency. They must ensure that accepted reports are visible on the public map and summary table, respecting anonymity settings chosen by citizens.

branch_003.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Coordinate Issue Resolution' accurately captures the functional intention of the External Maintenance Personnel actor as described in Section B (Case 1). The text explicitly states that these personnel can move reports from 'Assigned' to 'In Progress', exchange information/comments with the technical office, and mark reports as 'resolved'. This constitutes coordinating the resolution of the issue. The goal is supported by the documentation, reasonably scoped to the actor's responsibilities, and faithful to the project description. The reconstructed goal focuses heavily on 'transparency' and 'communication' which are means to an end, whereas the original goal correctly identifies the primary business outcome (resolving the issue) facilitated by that coordination. Therefore, the original goal should be kept. The current LLGs are incomplete and partially inconsistent with the project description. 
1. Incompleteness: The parent HLG 'Coordinate Issue Resolution' implies a two-way collaboration. The current LLGs only cover the external personnel's actions (updating status, marking resolved) but miss the critical communication aspect mentioned in the description: 'Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report'. This exchange is a key part of 'coordinating' and 'maintaining communication'.
2. Inconsistency/Misleading: The LLG 'Complete Report Resolution' states it notifies 'citizens'. However, the description explicitly states that comments and internal exchanges are 'not visible to the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens)'. While the citizen receives a notification of the state change (via email/platform notification as per section C), the LLG description implies a direct notification from the resolution action itself which might be misleading regarding the content visibility. More importantly, the 'Coordinate' aspect is missing the municipal operator's side of the interaction (assigning, commenting).
3. Scope: The parent HLG is about 'collaboration'. The current LLGs are purely operational steps for the external actor. They do not fully decompose the 'collaboration' goal, which involves both parties. Therefore, they are too narrow and incomplete.

To correctly decompose 'Coordinate Issue Resolution', you must include goals that reflect the bidirectional nature of the collaboration described in Case 1. Specifically, add an LLG for 'Exchange Comments/Information' between external personnel and municipal operators, as this is explicitly stated as a way to maintain communication. Also, ensure the 'Update Status' LLG clarifies that this is part of the workflow coordination. The 'Complete Report Resolution' LLG should be refined to ensure it doesn't imply direct citizen communication of internal details, but rather the finalization of the task which triggers the system's standard notification process.

branch_004.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Manage System Configuration and Report Assignment' is well-supported by the project description. Section B explicitly mentions that 'Automatic assignment... is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator,' linking configuration to assignment logic. Section D mentions a 'private section, accessible only to administrators' for statistics, implying administrative oversight. The goal accurately captures the two main responsibilities of the 'Municipal Administrators' actor described in the prompt: configuring system settings (specifically regarding external company assignments) and overseeing the assignment/management of reports. It is not too generic, nor is it unsupported. The bottom-up reconstruction is vaguer ('Enhance the management...') and less precise than the original. Therefore, the original goal should be kept. The current LLGs are incomplete and partially misleading regarding the scope of the Parent HLG. 
1. Incompleteness: The Parent HLG explicitly mentions 'Report Assignment'. The current LLG 'Assign Reports to Operators' only covers assignment to municipal operators. The project description specifies that reports can also be assigned to external companies (Case 1) and that automatic assignment rules can be configured by administrators. The current LLGs do not cover the configuration of these assignment rules or the assignment to external entities.
2. Misleading/Too Narrow: The LLG 'Configure System Settings' is too vague. The project description highlights specific configuration needs, such as enabling automatic assignment for external companies and managing notification preferences. The current description does not reflect the specific operational impact of these configurations on the report lifecycle.
3. Missing Goal: There is no LLG for managing the configuration of external company access or automatic assignment rules, which is a key part of 'optimizing operational efficiency' mentioned in the HLG description.

low_level_evaluation.regeneration_feedback:
The current LLGs fail to fully decompose the HLG. Specifically:
1. 'Assign Reports to Operators' is too narrow; it should encompass assigning reports to both municipal staff and external companies, or be split to reflect the different assignment mechanisms (manual vs. automatic).
2. 'Configure System Settings' is too generic. It should be refined to specifically address the configuration of report categories, notification channels, and crucially, the automatic assignment rules for external companies as described in section B.

branch_001.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Facilitate Citizen Reporting' accurately captures the core functional intention of the Citizens actor as described in the project description (Section A). The description explicitly details the process of registration and report submission (selecting location, filling forms, attaching photos). The goal is supported by the text, reasonably scoped to the actor's primary contribution, and faithful to the reconstruction. It is not too generic, ambiguous, or incorrectly scoped. Therefore, it should be kept. The current LLGs are incomplete and too operational. 
1. Incomplete: The HLG 'Facilitate Citizen Reporting' implies the entire process of reporting. The current LLGs miss critical steps defined in the requirements: 
   - Registration requires email confirmation (LLG 'Register User' only mentions creating an account, missing the validation step which is a prerequisite for using the system).
   - The report submission requires mandatory photos (LLG 'Attach Photos' exists but is separate; however, the flow is fragmented).
   - Most importantly, the HLG is about 'Reporting', but the current LLGs treat 'Login' as a primary goal. While login is necessary, the core value is the submission. 
   - The current LLGs are a list of atomic actions (API calls) rather than user goals. For example, 'Enter Report Title' and 'Select Category' are sub-steps of 'Compose Report'. 
2. Too Operational: Descriptions like 'through a registration API' or 'through a report title and description API' are implementation details, not user goals. Goals should be 'Register Account', 'Compose Report', 'Submit Report'.
3. Missing Context: The HLG mentions 'streamlined and user-friendly interface'. The current LLGs do not reflect the user's perspective of filling out a form or interacting with a map as a cohesive task.

Therefore, the LLGs need to be regenerated to better reflect the user's high-level goals (Register, Compose, Submit) and include the necessary validation steps (Confirm Registration) to be complete. LLG regeneration limit reached; keeping the latest LLGs.

branch_002.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Efficient Report Management' accurately captures the core functional intention of the Municipal Operators as described in the project description. The text details the entire lifecycle of a report (review, assignment, status updates, resolution) which constitutes 'management'. The goal is supported by the documentation (Section B and C), is reasonably scoped to the actor's responsibilities, and is not overly generic or ambiguous. The reconstructed goal focuses heavily on 'communication and tracking', which are means to an end, whereas the original goal correctly identifies the end state (management/resolution). Therefore, the original goal should be kept. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) are significantly flawed for several reasons:
1. **Too Operational/Technical**: Almost all LLGs explicitly mention 'via an API call'. LLGs should describe the functional goal from the user's perspective, not the technical implementation mechanism. This violates the abstraction level of LLGs.
2. **Incomplete Decomposition**: The parent HLG is 'Efficient Report Management'. The current LLGs miss critical steps in the report lifecycle described in the project description, specifically the initial 'Preliminary Review' (Accept/Reject) by the Organization Office, which is the first step in management. They also miss the specific handling of 'Suspended' states or the mandatory written explanation for rejections.
3. **Unsupported/Invented Features**: Several LLGs introduce features not present in the requirements:
   - 'Set Deadline for Citizen Report Resolution': The requirements do not mention setting deadlines.
   - 'Escalate Overdue Citizen Reports': The requirements do not mention escalation mechanisms.
   - 'Generate Report Summary': While statistics exist, the specific goal of generating a summary report via API is not a distinct management goal defined in the text; statistics are a separate section (D).
4. **Misleading Scope**: 'Communicate with External Company' is too narrow. The requirements specify that communication happens *through* the report (comments) and that external companies might not even have access (Case 2). The goal should be broader, such as 'Manage External Collaboration' or 'Update Report via External Feedback'.

Therefore, the LLGs need to be regenerated to align with the actual workflow (Review -> Assign -> Track -> Resolve) and remove technical constraints and unsupported features. LLG regeneration limit reached; keeping the latest LLGs.

low_level_evaluation.regeneration_feedback:
1. Remove all references to 'via an API call' from the descriptions. LLGs should focus on the user's intent and the system's functional response, not the interface protocol.
2. Add a goal for the initial review process: 'Review and Validate Citizen Report' (covering Accept/Reject decisions and mandatory rejection explanations).
3. Refine 'Assign Citizen Report' to reflect the logic of assigning to technical offices or external companies based on category.
4. Remove 'Set Deadline' and 'Escalate Overdue' as these are not supported by the requirements.
5. Refine 'Communicate with External Company' to 'Manage External Company Interaction' or similar, covering both cases (with and without system access) and the internal comment exchange.
6. Ensure 'Update Citizen Report Status' covers the full lifecycle states (Pending, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Resolved, Rejected).
7. Consider if 'Retrieve' and 'Search' are necessary as distinct LLGs or if they are sub-goals of 'Manage Reports'. Given the HLG is 'Efficient Management', searching and retrieving are enablers, but the core management actions are Review, Assign, Update Status, and Communicate. However, keeping 'Search' is acceptable if framed as 'Locate Reports for Management'.

branch_003.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Coordinate Issue Resolution' accurately captures the functional intention of the External Maintenance Personnel actor as described in Section B (Case 1). The text explicitly states that these personnel can move reports from 'Assigned' to 'In Progress', exchange information/comments with the technical office, and mark reports as 'resolved'. This constitutes coordinating the resolution of the issue. The goal is supported by the documentation, reasonably scoped to the actor's responsibilities, and faithful to the project description. The reconstructed goal focuses heavily on 'transparency' and 'communication' which are means to an end, whereas the original goal correctly identifies the primary business outcome (resolving the issue) facilitated by that coordination. Therefore, the original goal should be kept. The current LLGs are incomplete and partially inconsistent with the project description. 
1. Incompleteness: The parent HLG 'Coordinate Issue Resolution' implies a two-way collaboration. The current LLGs only cover the external personnel's actions (updating status, marking resolved) but miss the critical communication aspect mentioned in the description: 'Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report'. This exchange is a key part of 'coordinating' and 'maintaining communication'.
2. Inconsistency/Misleading: The LLG 'Complete Report Resolution' states it notifies 'citizens'. However, the description explicitly states that comments and internal exchanges are 'not visible to the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens)'. While the citizen receives a notification of the state change (via email/platform notification as per section C), the LLG description implies a direct notification from the resolution action itself which might be misleading regarding the content visibility. More importantly, the 'Coordinate' aspect is missing the municipal operator's side of the interaction (assigning, commenting).
3. Scope: The parent HLG is about 'collaboration'. The current LLGs are purely operational steps for the external actor. They do not fully decompose the 'collaboration' goal, which involves both parties. Therefore, they are too narrow and incomplete.

To correctly decompose 'Coordinate Issue Resolution', you must include goals that reflect the bidirectional nature of the collaboration described in Case 1. branch_004.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Manage System Configuration and Report Assignment' is well-supported by the project description. Section B explicitly mentions that 'Automatic assignment... is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator,' linking configuration to assignment logic. Section D mentions a 'private section, accessible only to administrators' for statistics, implying administrative oversight. The goal accurately captures the two main responsibilities of the 'Municipal Administrators' actor described in the prompt: configuring system settings (specifically regarding external company assignments) and overseeing the assignment/management of reports. It is not too generic, nor is it unsupported. The bottom-up reconstruction is vaguer ('Enhance the management...') and less precise than the original. Therefore, the original goal should be kept. The current LLGs are incomplete and partially misleading regarding the scope of the Parent HLG. 
1. Incompleteness: The Parent HLG explicitly mentions 'Report Assignment'. The current LLG 'Assign Reports to Operators' only covers assignment to municipal operators. The project description specifies that reports can also be assigned to external companies (Case 1) and that automatic assignment rules can be configured by administrators. The current LLGs do not cover the configuration of these assignment rules or the assignment to external entities.
2. Misleading/Too Narrow: The LLG 'Configure System Settings' is too vague. The project description highlights specific configuration needs, such as enabling automatic assignment for external companies and managing notification preferences. The current description does not reflect the specific operational impact of these configurations on the report lifecycle.
3. Missing Goal: There is no LLG for managing the configuration of external company access or automatic assignment rules, which is a key part of 'optimizing operational efficiency' mentioned in the HLG description.

branch_001.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Facilitate Citizen Reporting' accurately captures the core functional intention of the Citizens actor as described in the project description. The text explicitly details the registration and report submission process (Section A), which constitutes the primary interaction for this actor. The goal is supported by the documentation, reasonably scoped to the actor's main purpose, and not overly generic or ambiguous. The reconstructed goal is essentially a paraphrase of the original, so no rewriting is necessary. The current LLGs are incomplete and too operational. 
1. Incomplete: The HLG 'Facilitate Citizen Reporting' implies the entire process of reporting. The current LLGs miss critical steps defined in the requirements: 
   - Registration requires email confirmation (LLG 'Register User' only mentions creating an account, missing the validation step which is a prerequisite for using the system).
   - The report submission requires mandatory photos (LLG 'Attach Photos' exists but is separate; however, the flow is fragmented).
   - Most importantly, the HLG is about 'Reporting', but the current LLGs treat 'Login' as a primary goal. While login is necessary, the core value is the submission. 
   - The current LLGs are a list of atomic actions (API calls) rather than user goals. For example, 'Enter Report Title' and 'Select Category' are sub-steps of 'Compose Report'. 
2. Too Operational: Descriptions like 'through a registration API' or 'through a report title and description API' are implementation details, not user goals. Goals should be 'Register Account', 'Compose Report', 'Submit Report'.
3. Missing Context: The HLG mentions 'accessibility and ease of use'. The current LLGs do not reflect the user-centric nature of the interaction (e.g., selecting a point on a map is a key part of the 'ease of use' for location, but it's buried in a technical API description).

Therefore, the LLGs need to be regenerated to better reflect the user's high-level goals (Register, Compose, Submit) and ensure all mandatory steps (like email confirmation) are captured as part of the registration goal or a distinct validation goal if necessary, though typically 'Register' implies the successful completion of the process. The current decomposition is too granular and technical. LLG regeneration limit reached; keeping the latest LLGs.

branch_002.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Efficient Report Management' accurately captures the core functional intention of the Municipal Operators as described in the project description. The text details the entire lifecycle of a report (review, assignment, status updates, resolution) which constitutes 'management'. The goal is supported by the documentation (Section B and C), is reasonably scoped to the actor's responsibilities, and is not overly generic or ambiguous. The reconstructed goal focuses heavily on 'communication and tracking', which are means to an end, whereas the original goal correctly identifies the end state (management/resolution). Therefore, the original goal should be kept. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) are significantly flawed for several reasons:
1. **Too Operational/Technical**: Almost all LLGs explicitly mention 'via an API call'. LLGs should describe the functional goal from the user's perspective, not the technical implementation mechanism. This violates the abstraction level of LLGs.
2. **Incomplete Decomposition**: The parent HLG is 'Efficient Report Management'. The current LLGs miss critical steps in the report lifecycle described in the project description, specifically the initial 'Preliminary Review' (Accept/Reject) by the Organization Office, which is the first step in management. They also miss the specific handling of 'Suspended' states or the mandatory written explanation for rejections.
3. **Unsupported/Invented Features**: Several LLGs introduce features not present in the requirements:
   - 'Set Deadline for Citizen Report Resolution': The requirements do not mention setting deadlines.
   - 'Escalate Overdue Citizen Reports': The requirements do not mention escalation mechanisms.
   - 'Generate Report Summary': While statistics exist, the specific goal of generating a summary report via API is not a distinct management goal defined in the text; statistics are a separate section (D).
4. **Misleading Scope**: 'Communicate with External Company' is too narrow. The requirements specify that communication happens *through* the report (comments) and that external companies might not even have access (Case 2). The goal should be broader, such as 'Manage External Collaboration' or 'Update Report via External Feedback'.

Therefore, the LLGs need to be regenerated to align with the actual workflow (Review -> Assign -> Track -> Resolve) and remove technical constraints and unsupported features. LLG regeneration limit reached; keeping the latest LLGs.

low_level_evaluation.regeneration_feedback:
1. Remove all references to 'via an API call' from the descriptions. LLGs should focus on the user's intent and the system's functional response, not the interface protocol.
2. Add a goal for the initial review process: 'Review and Validate Citizen Report' (covering Accept/Reject decisions and mandatory rejection explanations).
3. Refine 'Assign Citizen Report' to reflect the logic of assigning to technical offices or external companies based on category.
4. Remove 'Set Deadline' and 'Escalate Overdue' as these are not supported by the requirements.
5. Refine 'Communicate with External Company' to 'Manage External Company Interaction' or similar, covering both cases (with and without system access) and the internal comment exchange.
6. Ensure 'Update Citizen Report Status' covers the full lifecycle states (Pending, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Resolved, Rejected).
7. Consider if 'Retrieve' and 'Search' are necessary as distinct LLGs or if they are sub-goals of 'Manage Reports'. Given the HLG is 'Efficient Management', searching and retrieving are enablers, but the core management actions are Review, Assign, Update Status, and Communicate. However, keeping 'Search' is acceptable if framed as 'Locate Reports for Management'.

branch_003.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Coordinate Issue Resolution' accurately captures the functional intention described in Section B (Case 1) of the project description. The text explicitly states that external maintenance personnel can move reports from 'Assigned' to 'In Progress', exchange information and comments with the technical office, and mark reports as resolved. This constitutes a coordination process to resolve issues. The goal is supported by the documentation, correctly scoped to the actor's responsibilities, and is not too generic or ambiguous. The reconstructed goal is less precise regarding the collaborative aspect ('coordinate') which is a key feature mentioned (exchanging information). Therefore, the original goal should be kept. The current LLGs are incomplete and partially inconsistent with the project description. Specifically: 1) The HLG aims to 'Coordinate Issue Resolution' and 'maintain communication'. The current LLGs miss the critical step of transitioning the issue from 'Assigned' to 'In Progress' (Work in Progress), which is explicitly stated in Case 1 ('External maintenance personnel can move the report from Assigned to In Progress'). The current 'Accept Assigned Issue' is vague and not explicitly defined in the text, whereas the status change is. 2) The 'Update Issue Status' LLG is too broad and overlaps with 'Complete Report Resolution'. The text specifies that external personnel can mark the report as 'resolved'. 3) The 'Exchange Comments/Information' LLG is correct but needs to be precise about the audience (internal team only, not citizens). 4) The current set lacks the specific action of starting the work (moving to In Progress), which is a key part of the coordination workflow described. Therefore, regeneration is needed to align strictly with the 'Case 1' workflow: View -> Move to In Progress -> Communicate -> Mark Resolved.

The text states: 'External maintenance personnel can move the report from Assigned to In Progress... Once the work is completed, the external maintainer can mark the report as resolved.' The 'Complete Report Resolution' and 'Update Issue Status' are redundant or imprecise. The 'Accept' step is not in the text. Please regenerate to match these four specific actions.

branch_001.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Facilitate Citizen Reporting' accurately captures the core functional intention of the Citizens actor as described in the project description. The text explicitly details the registration and report submission process (Section A), which constitutes the primary interaction for this actor. The goal is supported by the documentation, reasonably scoped to the actor's main purpose, and not overly generic or ambiguous. The reconstructed goal is essentially a paraphrase of the original, so no rewriting is necessary. The current LLGs are incomplete and too operational. 
1. Incomplete: The HLG 'Facilitate Citizen Reporting' implies the entire process of reporting. The current LLGs miss critical steps defined in the requirements: 
   - Registration requires email confirmation (LLG 'Register User' only mentions creating an account, missing the validation step which is a prerequisite for using the system).
   - The report submission requires mandatory photos (LLG 'Attach Photos' exists but is separate; however, the flow is fragmented).
   - Most importantly, the HLG is about 'Reporting', but the current LLGs treat 'Login' as a primary goal. While login is necessary, the core value is the submission. 
   - The current LLGs are a list of atomic actions (API calls) rather than user goals. For example, 'Enter Report Title' and 'Select Category' are sub-steps of 'Compose Report'. 
2. Too Operational: Descriptions like 'through a registration API' or 'through a report title and description API' are implementation details, not user goals. Goals should be 'Register Account', 'Compose Report', 'Submit Report'.
3. Missing Context: The HLG mentions 'accessibility and ease of use'. The current LLGs do not reflect the user-centric nature of the interaction (e.g., selecting a point on a map is a key part of the 'ease of use' for location, but it's buried in a technical API description).

Therefore, the LLGs need to be regenerated to better reflect the user's high-level goals (Register, Compose, Submit) and ensure all mandatory steps (like email confirmation) are captured as part of the registration goal or a distinct validation goal if necessary, though typically 'Register' implies the successful completion of the process. The current decomposition is too granular and technical. LLG regeneration limit reached; keeping the latest LLGs.
